page: Microsoft Azure D96s_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, supplying 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory allocation is balanced at 384.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The processor features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes no bundled local storage and has no integrated GPUs.

Benchmark measurements reveal high-capacity parallel compute and memory bandwidth capabilities. In multi-threaded evaluations, the server achieves top-quartile performance, including a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 93,245.95, a PassMark CPU score of 76,512.7, and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 17,760.0. Cryptographic performance sits in the top decile with a PassMark encryption score of 87,443.15, supported by hardware-accelerated instructions. Memory bandwidth is pronounced, testing at 323.4 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 131.45 GB/sec for writes. Conversely, single-threaded metrics such as single-core stress-ng (1,899.87) and single-core Geekbench (1,699.0) sit within the middle 50% percentile.

In operational benchmark tests, the instance demonstrated strong database processing, reaching 30,812.47 PassMark database operations and 87.92 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside 63.83 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Because it lacks discrete GPUs, larger AI workloads show limited throughput, dropping to 2.72 tokens per second for text generation on a 70B parameter LLM. The absence of local disk requires external networked block storage for persistent data. Microsoft Azure D96s_v5 is suited for parallel compilation, enterprise web applications, in-memory caching tiers, database servers, and multi-threaded batch data processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D96s_v5 is a general-purpose instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor at 2.8 GHz, paired with 384.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks local storage and discrete GPUs, relying on remote storage architectures. In benchmarks, it delivers top-tier parallel compute, high-throughput cryptographic processing, and strong memory bandwidth, though single-core performance remains in the middle percentile tier. The 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio and multi-threaded scaling make it effective for large databases, Redis caching, software compilation, and high-concurrency web services.
